title: CharIN Megawatt Charging System: 4th Event Summary Report
authors: Isaac Tolbert; Namrata Kogalur; Jonathan Martin; Andrew Meintz
locator: May 2024 report, §§3.2.1–3.2.5, printed pp. 25–30; separate NOTICE at front.
finding: Three force transducers, three insertion/two withdrawal position transducers and seven wired contact channels. After all pins conducted, locking-pin insertion independently confirmed full seating. Of 12 hardware pairs, 11 mated; prose reports 6 passed insertion-force and 5 withdrawal-force tests, with 3 passing both. Authors selected the three most consistent runs per pair. PP withdrawal coordinates required a clamp-slip correction.
rights: Public DOE technical report. Front NOTICE restricts reuse/dissemination of figures and tables. Only original annotations and counts inferred from narrative are provided.

title: Simulation and experimental verification of electrical contact resistance of heavy-duty connectors with axially canted coil springs socket assembly
authors: Chao Zhang; Hongcheng Chen; Wanbin Ren; Jian Liu
locator: February 2026 version of record; Results and discussion, narrative at Figs. 10–12; ref. 37.
finding: A 1 mm/s insertion test used imaging, axial force and electrical contact resistance. Three successive spring engagements increased stable force while stable resistance fell. Force drops after local peaks do not uniquely indicate full engagement. Reported stage values only; no release of synchronous per-sample arrays verified.
rights: CC BY-NC 4.0. Authors retain copyright. This batch stores original calculated summaries of three reported stage values.

title: Investigation on failure mechanism of electrical connectors under repetitive mechanical insertion and withdrawal operations
locator: IOP conference paper, vol. 1207, 012011. Public full-text mirror, pp. 2–5, Figs. 1–5.
finding: Slide-table plug force and four-wire resistance were acquired simultaneously. A typical insertion had a force maximum near 12 N and subsequent stable force near 8 N while resistance stayed approximately stable. In repeated cycling, electrical and mechanical changes emerged after 15,000 cycles. One plotted trace and a life-test trend answer different questions.
rights: Public IOP conference paper; original factual annotations only.

title: Mechanical Insertion Force and Electrical Contact Resistance of By-Pass Switches with Axially Canted Coil Springs
authors: Chao Zhang; Ming Li; Wanbin Ren; Jian Liu
locator: September 2025 version of record; numerical results and conclusion.
finding: Analytical/finite-element precursor models a by-pass switch. Its conclusion leaves experimental validation for future work. The adjacent experimentally instrumented socket study cites this paper.

title: Evolution of contact performance of industry electrical connector based on reliability accelerated testing
authors: Jing Ni; Lidong Han; Jianfeng Pan; Junqiang Zheng; Yu Shi; Zhi Cui; Jun Cai
locator: 2021 version of record; experimental system and operating conditions, Figs. 1–3.
finding: CDSM-0.75 connector study examines mating forces, electrical resistance and wear. A 10,240 Hz DAQ and a piezoelectric sensor specified at 20 Hz frequency response are distinct parts of the instrument chain. Repeated readings were averaged; the DAQ frequency does not establish equal bandwidth or synchronization of the resistance tester.

title: Integrated design of insertions-extractions performance and contact reliability of spring-wire socket electrical connector
authors: Ping Qian; Qiqi Chen; Chi Chen; Jun Pan; Kunkun Han
locator: 2024 version of record; Parameter estimation, Figs. 4–6 and Table 2.
finding: At 20 °C, ten contacts were tested for 1,000 insertion/extraction cycles with four-wire readings every 100 cycles. Resistance is the mean of three measurements. The 240 h between 100-cycle groups also admits storage effects. Table 2 provides model parameters; it does not provide transient axial force or per-stroke trajectories.

title: In-Situ Fretting Wear Analysis of Electrical Connectors for Real System Applications
authors: Arpith Siddaiah; Ashish K. Kasar; Vishal Khosla; Pradeep L. Menezes
locator: 2019 version of record; experimental setup, Figs. 2–4.
finding: Fretting test of an existing Ag-coated connector interface. Four-wire resistance, normal load, tangential force amplitude, wear and motion were recorded with a 5 kHz acquisition system. Evidence concerns small post-contact motions rather than full connector seating.

title: Six-axis Force–Torque Analysis of a Flexible-Tube Wrist for Misaligned Ports in Robotic EV Charging
authors: Raihan Yusuf Rifansyah; Agus Heri Setya Budi; Hendri Maja Saputra
locator: Vol. 17(2), pp. 62–69, §II.A, §II.C, Fig. 7 and references [15–16]. DOI printed by publisher; Crossref works endpoint returned 404.
finding: The investigators removed the electrical pins from the type-2 receptacle. An upstream AFT200 six-axis sensor supplied profiles; onset was marked visually on an average of ten trials per condition. Reported onset shifts from 45.8 mm at zero angle to 31.8 mm at +8° yaw. An independent electrical-contact outcome cannot be recovered from this setup.
rights: CC BY-SA 4.0. Public full text, annotations only.

authors: Hendri Maja Saputra; Ahmad Pahrurrozi; Catur Hilman Adritya Haryo Bhakti Baskoro; Nur Safwati Mohd Nor; Nanang Ismail; Estiko Rijanto; Edwar Yazid; Mohd Zarhamdy Md Zain; Intan Zaurah Mat Darus

finding: The three-axis flexible-tube force prediction study describes 17,293 rows and plots a 250-sample comparison. The 2025 six-axis paper identifies this as the same flexible tube. A predicted force and an independent latch confirmation are different observations.

title: Characterization of plugging and unplugging process for electric vehicle charging connectors based on Force/Torque measurements
authors: Hendri Maja Saputra; Nur Safwati Mohd Nor; Estiko Rijanto; Ahmad Pahrurrozi; Catur Hilman A.H.B. Baskoro; Edwar Yazid; Mohd Zarhamdy Md Zain; Intan Zaurah Mat Darus
locator: Publisher abstract and highlights, Measurement vol. 242, art. 115876; January 2025 issue.
finding: Forty human operators contribute force/torque observations of plugging and unplugging. Abstract gives impulses of 74.15 and 57.92 N·s. No primary downloadable trial file verified; population and measurement differ from robot trials.
rights: Publisher abstract screened; no source material copied.

title: Investigation on Intermittent Failure Phenomenon of Electrical Connectors Under Repetitive Mechanical Insertion and Withdrawal Operations
authors: Yuan Meng; Wanbin Ren; Chao Zhang
locator: 2022 journal record and public abstract. Compare same authors and subject with 2021 IOP report.
finding: An intermittent-failure follow-up examines connector contact resistance under repeated insertion/withdrawal. The two publications are retained separately. Independence of the experimental records is unverified.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Industrial Insertion Tasks with Visual Inputs and Natural Rewards
authors: Gerrit Schoettler; Ashvin Nair; Jianlan Luo; Shikhar Bahl; Juan Aparicio Ojea; Eugen Solowjow; Sergey Levine
locator: arXiv v2 dated 2019-08-02, §§5.2–5.4, Fig. 6; same-title earlier workshop copy Table 1 and bibliography. Year field gives 2020 IROS proceedings year.
finding: Real Sawyer setup uses electrical-connection detection for a sparse USB reward. A goal-image reward can be improved by moving in front of or behind the socket. Electrical connection was only automatically measured for USB. Across 25 executions per condition, residual sparse SAC success fell from 88% to 84% under ±1 mm perturbations; residual sparse TD3 fell from 100% to 36%.
rights: Public original author copies; only study facts and authored contrasts.

title: Localization and manipulation of small parts using GelSight tactile sensing
authors: Rui Li; Robert Platt; Wenzhen Yuan; Andreas ten Pas; Nathan Roscup; Mandayam A. Srinivasan; Edward Adelson
finding: Baxter succeeded in 34/36 subsequent insertions after a successful tactile localization. Grasps without valid localization were excluded. Entry sufficiently far for continued downward pressure to complete mating counted as success. Neither full seating nor electrical continuity is verified by that count.
rights: Public author or proceedings copy. No redistribution grant established here; source pointer and original observations only.

title: A Laser-based Dual-arm System for Precise Control of Collaborative Robots
authors: Joao Silverio; Guillaume Clivaz; Sylvain Calinon
locator: Author preprint arXiv:2011.01573v2 dated 2021-03-25, §V, Table II and Figs. 8–9.
finding: Two Panda arms with laser scanning for plug/socket registration. Ten USB insertions per tested setup gave 90% (IC1) and 0% (IC2) using proprioception only and 100% with scan correction. The scanner corrects relative pose; electrical contact is not independently logged in the cited evidence.
rights: Public author or proceedings copy. No redistribution grant established here; source pointer and original observations only.

title: Robot, feed thyself: Plugging in to unmodified electrical outlets by sensing emitted AC electric fields
authors: Brian Mayton; Louis LeGrand; Joshua R Smith
locator: 2010 ICRA paper, Results, 30 trials. Public full text in Academia copy 117411502 and indexed CiteSeerX PDF (direct PDF download returned HTTP 404).
finding: Robot used the 60 Hz electric field for alignment and succeeded in 28 of 30 attempts. Pre-contact electrical-field sensing is a localization modality. This fraction does not provide separate seven-pin continuity and latch time series.
rights: Public author or proceedings copy. No redistribution grant established here; source pointer and original observations only.

title: Experimental and Analytical Studies of the Connector Insertion Phase
locator: December 2008 journal record and public abstract.
finding: Laser-measured spring deflection provides an indirect contact-force estimate alongside insertion force and resistance. Per-trial data and numerical calibration uncertainty were not verified.
rights: IEEE abstract and indexed authors only.
